title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: A universal method to check if a Field has a value in AL
summary: The post explains how to universally check if a field contains a value in Business Central AL code using the HasValue procedure from the Change Log Management codeunit, which works across different data types without needing type-specific validation syntax.
key_points: Business Central provides the HasValue procedure in codeunit 423 Change Log Management as a standard method for checking field values
The method accepts a FieldRef parameter, making it work universally across all data types
This approach eliminates the need for different validation syntax for different field types like Integer, Date, or Decimal
The example demonstrates checking a Customer Name field by opening the Customer table, getting a field reference, and calling HasValue

quotes.text: Microsoft actually provides a standard method to address this.
quotes.why_it_matters: Directs developers to use the built-in HasValue procedure instead of writing custom validation code

quotes.text: All we need is to pass the FieldRef as a parameter.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the simplicity of the universal approach that works for any field type
